entities.summary:
Giovanni Poggio (1493–1556) was a prominent Italian Roman Catholic cardinal and diplomat whose career spanned the volatile decades of the early Counter-Reformation and the Italian Wars. Born in Bologna, Poggio rose through the ecclesiastical ranks, serving as Archbishop of Lucca and later as Cardinal-Priest of Santa Susanna. His significance lies not only in his extensive diplomatic service, which included pivotal nunciatures to Spain and England, but also in his patronage of the arts, particularly the elaborate transformation of his Bologna residence, the Palazzo Poggi, into a showcase of Renaissance artistic and architectural ideals.

Poggio's diplomatic career was marked by his service to Popes Clement VII and Paul III during a period of immense political and religious upheaval. As Papal Nuncio to Spain from 1529 to 1541, he played a crucial role in mediating relations between the Holy See and Emperor Charles V, navigating the complexities of the Reformation's spread and the ongoing Italian Wars. He also served briefly as Nuncio to England in 1544, though his efforts there were overshadowed by the deepening schism under Henry VIII. Later, as a cardinal, Poggio participated in the initial sessions of the Council of Trent, contributing to the foundational discussions that would shape the Catholic Church's response to Protestantism.
